name: sandbox-enforce
description: The sandbox@1 provider `local-os`: the ENFORCING half of the confinement seam. It probes the host for the strongest mechanism it has (bwrap mount/pid/net namespaces, unshare -n, prlimit, the /bin/sh ulimit prologue, setpriv) and runs a command under the decision of the shared policy engine: confined filesystem roots, denied network egress, a filtered environment, a pinned cwd, kernel resource ceilings, a deadline that signals the whole process group and inline byte caps. Every constraint it cannot enforce is reported as a gap. Declares execution/policies because it starts host processes.

config.description: The SAME policy shape as core/sandbox-policy (source, unconfigured, defaults, resources, approvalRequired) plus the runner knobs below: this provider decides and enforces, so a deployment mounts exactly one of the two.

source.description: Label of this policy, reported by `sandbox policy` (default sandbox@1).

unconfigured.description: What a resource with NO rule and NO defaults gets: `deny` (fail-closed) or `allow`.

approvalRequired.description: Every call needs an explicit approval (a call without approvalGranted is denied and runs nothing).

defaults.description: The rule every resource starts from (mode, readRoots, writeRoots, env NAME allow-list, network, limits, approvalRequired, dropPrivileges, allowCommands, denyCommands, deny).

resources.description: One rule per resource NAME (fs, subprocess, jobs, computer-use, browser-use, or a custom name); `deny: true` refuses the resource outright.

shell.description: Shell used by the `ulimit` rlimit fallback and by the mechanism probe.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline of a run when neither the call nor the policy names one (the policy cap always wins).

maxOutputBytes.description: Inline byte cap of a run when neither the call nor the policy names one (the policy cap always wins).
